title: GI Metal aluminum peel
text:
GI Metal aluminum peel. Here's an update. I exchanged the first one via Amazon and their seller and was sent a replacement same model. I made 3 pizzas for friends this past Friday night. I was extra careful not to let it in the 800 degree oven for too l long. It too ended the night with some discoloration but not as bad as the first one. I'm tired of this so as long as it stays structurally sound I will ignore the discoloring but would suggest that any prospective buyers consider GI's stainless steel peel I now wish I had. My experience with GI's stainless steel turning peel is excellent.

First purchase review: I used it once very fast and the peel the part that holds the pizza has already discolored some. I had the other one with the slots but the problems is the wet dough sticks and drops into the holes so I decided to get this one from the same company, GI Metal . I just don't think it should discolor from moving in and taking out 1 pizza. I also have the 9" turning peel from GI and have used many times and still looks new so be careful or check with Amazon first before you consider this peel. I'm hoping the company that sold it to me will reach out and explain. I buy a lot from Amazon and rarely have issues with any of my purchases.

product_metadata.title: Professional 13-inch Rectangle Pizza Peel with 47-inch Handle
features: Made in Italy for Professional Use. 13 inch head/47 inch handle
Milled, beveled edge make it easier to get under the pizza
ERGONOMIC. The handles have an oval tubular design to increase stability.
Stong and durable with manufacturer warranty
description: Strong and Light: All models have strong and lightweight peel handles that are oval and tubular. The tubular form makes them more stable, and the oval shape is easy to hold. Practical: Light, flexible aluminum heads allow for scraper effect to get under dough easily. Neutral anodizing process on head surface makes the surface even and protects it from oxidization. The milled beveled edge makes it easier to take hold of the pizza. Hard-wearing and secure riveted joint between the head and handle prevent vibration transmission to the handle. You can buy a carbon constructed or golden hardened anodized pizza peel for high performance use, but they are expensive ($200-300). You can buy a moderate use pizza peel (AMICA) that are inexpensive and cheap ($20-50), and they will need to be replaced often. Or you can buy this professional grade (Azzurra) pizza peel that is built to last for repeated use, moderately priced, and will last longer than the inexpensive pizza peels.
